title: OPcache & Route Bootstrap Evidence
hypothesis: PHP-FPM recompiles company.php every request because OPcache is disabled or ineffective
hypothesis_result: CONFIRMED — OPcache module is not loaded at all on PHP-FPM or CLI

why_disabled.explanation: The Zend OPcache shared object exists on disk (opcache.so) but is never loaded because zend_extension=opcache is commented out. All [opcache] settings below are also commented. conf.d and FPM pool do not re-enable it. Result: every request compiles PHP from source; no opcode cache hits possible.

opcache.pool_overrides: None for opcache. admin pool sets open_basedir, session.save_path, pm=ondemand only.

compile_vs_execute.conclusion: Wall time under FPM is dominated by EXECUTING ~1154 route registrations (~0.37 ms/route), not by lex/compile (~3 ms). Without OPcache, compile still repeats each request but is small vs execute cost under FPM.

sections.pattern: Uniform — 8 buckets of ~145 routes each ~50–59 ms
sections.implication: No single hot function inside company.php; cost is proportional to route count.

ttfb.note: FPM OPcache not enabled; TTFB unchanged from prior RCA (~550–670 ms warm)

forced_opcache_cli_sandbox.note: Fresh CLI process each run cannot show cross-request FPM cache hits; opcache_compile_file proves compile caches (2.8 ms → 0.001 ms) inside one process.

should_split_company_php.recommendation: DO NOT SPLIT for compile-time reasons alone
should_split_company_php.reason: opcache_compile_file of the 120 KB file is only ~2.8 ms. FPM spent ~430 ms mostly executing 1154 registrations. Splitting into multiple files without lazy-loading still runs the same registrations every request. Enabling OPcache addresses repeated compile; lazy/portal-scoped route loading would address execute cost — out of scope for Phase Y evidence.
